evaluation_claims.text: Rust is a reddish-orange to reddish-brown mixture of iron oxides associated with the corrosion of refined iron.
Rust consists of iron(III) oxide, various hydrous ferric oxides, and iron(III) oxide-hydroxide.
Rusting occurs when iron reacts with oxygen in the catalytic presence of water or air moisture.
Both oxygen and water are essential for rusting; iron left exposed to both over sufficient time can convert entirely into rust.
Unlike aluminum, copper, and tin, which develop stable oxide films, surface rust on iron is typically flaky and friable.
Rust offers no passivational protection to the underlying metal, allowing oxygen and moisture to penetrate deeper.
Rust occupies a much higher volume than the original iron.
Rust expansion can create internal stress that pushes adjacent mechanical parts apart, a phenomenon known as rust jacking.
Barrier protection physically isolates iron from its environment.
Barrier protection can involve waterproof coatings, paints, varnishes, oils, waxes, or plastic and metal foils.
In enclosed spaces, desiccants like silica gel can control moisture exposure.
Multi-coat barrier paint systems use a primer coat as an inhibitor, an intermediate coat for protective thickness, and a finish coat for environmental resistance.
Powders like epoxy, nylon, or urethane can be applied to adhere as a thin protective film.
Rust converters containing tannic acid or phosphoric acid can chemically transform surface rust into a protective layer ready for painting.
Alloying iron with metals such as chromium or nickel greatly improves its resistance to rust, as in stainless steel.
Alloyed steel is very expensive.
Cathodic protection works by converting active corrosion sites on a metal surface into passive sites by supplying electrons from another source.
Sacrificial galvanic anodes are commonly made of more reactive metals such as magnesium, aluminum, or zinc.
Because sacrificial metals are more reactive, they corrode first, preserving the underlying iron.
Galvanization coats iron or steel with a thin layer of zinc, often by immersion in molten zinc through hot-dip galvanizing.
The zinc layer both physically blocks water and oxygen and acts as sacrificial protection.
Anodic protection controls corrosion by making the metal surface the anode of an electrolytic cell.
Sacrificial anodes are consumed over time and require frequent inspection and replacement, raising long-term maintenance costs.
Attached sacrificial anodes add physical weight to structures and perform poorly in high-resistivity environments.

additional_metric_details.notes: All scores are Claude judgments, not verified ground truth. Repair effectiveness compares coverage/narration, not factual truth. No revision or no retrieval is N/A rather than zero.

metric_semantics.reference_evidence_support_percent: Evidence entailment within the frozen reference corpus; not factual accuracy.
metric_semantics.query_coverage_percent: Coverage of a fixed six-aspect checklist derived once per question from the question text and shared by all systems; missing/duplicate judge outputs are normalized against that fixed denominator.
metric_semantics.narration_input: Coverage, relevance, narration and grounded-requirement judgements use the complete script with [E-...] evidence markers removed; claim extraction and citation metrics use the marked script. Aspect scores are continuous in [0, 1].
metric_semantics.narration_quality_percent: Ten-dimension spoken educational narration score; excludes factual truth.
metric_semantics.citation_precision: Share of emitted citation IDs that are identified as supporting the claim when verification is restricted to cited passages.
metric_semantics.citation_recall: Share of all citation-required extracted factual claims that have at least one cited passage judged to support the claim.
